readings.reading: Four 3x3 shapes lie scattered on a large grid. The output is a 7x7 grid with each shape's 3x3 box copied unchanged into the quadrant matching its position (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), with one blank row and column between them.
readings.why: every pair has exactly four objects, each fitting a 3x3 box, and the output quadrants equal those boxes in positional order

readings.reading: Four 3x3 red shapes are scattered on a large grid. The output is 7x7: the four shapes laid out 2x2 with a one-cell gap, each keeping its quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) by relative position.
readings.why: every input object is 3x3; the output is exactly the four boxes placed by relative order with one blank row and column between them

readings.reading: Four 3x3 shapes lie scattered on the grid; the output is a 7x7 grid that packs them into a 2x2 layout (one empty row and column between) keeping their relative positions: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
readings.why: each output 3x3 slot equals the 3x3 box of the input object in that quadrant

readings.reading: Four 3x3 red shapes scattered on a large grid are gathered into a 7x7 grid: each shape keeps its pattern and goes to the quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) matching its relative position, with a 1-cell empty gap row/column between them.
readings.why: each output 3x3 corner block equals the bounding box of the input object lying in that relative quadrant

readings.reading: Four scattered 3x3 objects of one colour are gathered into a 7x7 grid as a 2x2 layout with a one-cell gap, each object keeping its shape and going to the quadrant matching its relative position (top/bottom, left/right).
readings.why: each output quadrant equals exactly one input object's 3x3 box, in the same relative arrangement

readings.reading: A wavy 1-coloured wall runs across the top, with notches open on its underside. A 5-coloured piece below turns 2 if some rotation of it, pushed up into one of the notches, fills that notch exactly. Pieces that fit no notch stay 5.
readings.why: on every pair, the recoloured pieces are exactly those whose rotated top matches a notch shape: 2x2 notches take a 2x2 block, P-pentomino or 2x2-topped shape; a T notch takes a T or a plus; a 1x2 notch takes a 1x3 bar

readings.reading: A blue structure on top has downward-opening cavities; grey pieces lie below. A grey piece turns red (2) if some rotation/reflection of it, pushed up from below, fills one cavity exactly (extra cells may stick out below the structure).
readings.why: on every pair the recoloured grey objects are exactly those that can plug a cavity; the rest stay grey

readings.reading: A colour-1 wall sits at the top with notches on its underside; each colour-5 piece below that (in some rotation or reflection) could plug one underside notch completely, with any extra cells hanging out below, is recoloured 2; other pieces stay 5.
readings.why: exactly the 5-pieces that can plug some underside notch become 2; nothing else changes

readings.verb: recolour shapes that plug a hole
readings.reading: Grey shapes below the blue shape turn red when some rotation/reflection of the shape can be pushed up into one of the blue shape's downward-open holes and fill that hole completely (any remainder hanging below the blue shape without touching blue); other grey shapes stay grey.
readings.why: every cell of a grey (5) shape that can fill a hole of the blue (1) shape becomes red (2); the blue shape and the non-fitting grey shapes are unchanged

readings.verb: recolour pieces that fit the lock
readings.reading: The colour-1 shape on top has downward-open cavities; every colour-5 piece below that could be slid up (rotation allowed) to completely fill one cavity is recoloured 2, the others stay 5.
readings.why: exactly the 5-pieces that can exactly fill some cavity of the 1-shape change to 2; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Single coloured cells (markers) each move to the nearest 2x2 5-block and stop on a cell touching it (side or corner). The blocks stay where they are.
readings.why: every marker ends 8-adjacent to a 5-block and keeps its colour; marker count and block positions do not change

readings.reading: Grey 2x2 blocks stay put. Each single coloured cell moves in a straight line (orthogonal preferred, else diagonal) to the nearest position touching a grey block.
readings.why: every coloured marker ends 8-adjacent to a grey block, reached by the shortest straight move; blocks do not change

readings.reading: Single coloured cells move to touch the nearest grey 2x2 block, landing on the nearest free cell adjacent (8-neighbour) to it; the grey blocks stay put.
readings.why: every single cell ends 8-adjacent to a grey block at the nearest free contact cell (a closer cell claims a contested spot first)

readings.reading: Each single coloured pixel slides in a straight (orthogonal or diagonal) line toward the nearest grey 2x2 block and stops at the first cell touching it (8-adjacency); the grey blocks stay.
readings.why: every 1-cell object keeps its colour and ends 8-adjacent to a grey (5) block, reached by a straight or diagonal path; markers are not usable as subject because some pixels touch each other

readings.reading: Each single coloured cell moves to the nearest 2x2 block of 5 and parks in the cell of the block's surrounding ring on its side (touching the block, edge or corner); the blocks stay.
readings.why: every dot keeps its colour and ends 8-adjacent to its nearest 5-block; nothing else changes

readings.reading: There are two markers, one in rows 0-4 and one in rows 5-9. Each half of the 10x10 grid gets a fixed pattern in its marker's colour: a full row through the marker row, the outer row of that half (row 0 or row 9), and the left and right border columns of that half.
readings.why: on both pairs the pattern is the same and depends only on the marker rows (2 and 7) and colours, not on the marker columns

readings.reading: Two single cells (top half, bottom half). The output draws a frame: the top half in the top cell's colour (full rows at row 0 and at the cell's row, side columns elsewhere), the bottom half in the bottom cell's colour (full rows at the cell's row and the last row, side columns elsewhere).
readings.why: every non-background output cell is on the border or a marker row, coloured by the marker in its half

readings.reading: Two coloured cells, one in the top half and one in the bottom half; the output draws a frame: the top half (rows 0-4) in the upper cell's colour with the outer top row and the cell's row filled full and side columns filled; the bottom half (rows 5-9) likewise in the lower cell's colour with its row and the bottom row full.
readings.why: every output cell is the colour of the seed of its half if it lies on the grid border or on that seed's row, else background

readings.reading: Two pixels (upper and lower) each draw a pattern in their own colour: the upper colour draws the top half (rows 0-4): full row 0, full row through the pixel, and both side columns; the lower colour draws the bottom half (rows 5-9): full row through the pixel, full last row, and both side columns.
readings.why: every non-empty output cell lies on a border row/column of its half or on the row of that half's pixel, coloured by that pixel

readings.reading: Two markers (one in the top half, one in the bottom half) each draw, in their own colour, the outline of their half of the grid (top row/bottom row and both side columns) plus a full horizontal line through the marker's row.
readings.why: every output cell of the half is marker colour exactly on its side columns, outer row and marker row

readings.reading: A 3x3 multi-coloured block sits on the background. Each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray in its own colour, pointing away from the block centre (corner cells go diagonally, edge cells straight), until it reaches the grid border. The centre cell stays.
readings.why: every ray starts at an outer cell of the block, runs in the direction from the centre to that cell, and ends at the border

readings.reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block; each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray of its own colour outward (corners diagonally, edges straight) to the grid border. The centre stays.
readings.why: every ray starts at an outer cell of the block, runs away from the block centre in that cell's direction, and reaches the border

readings.reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block: each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray in its own direction away from the centre (edges straight, corners diagonal) in its own colour until the grid border; the centre stays.
readings.why: every ray runs from an outer block cell outward along its direction from the block centre to the border, in that cell's colour

readings.reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block shoots rays: each of its 8 outer cells extends in its own colour away from the centre cell (edges straight, corners diagonally) to the grid border; the centre cell does not extend.
readings.why: every outer block cell continues as a straight line in the direction from the block centre through that cell until the border, in that cell's colour

readings.reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block shoots a ray from each of its 8 outer cells outward (edge cells straight, corner cells diagonally) in that cell's colour to the grid border; the centre cell emits nothing.
readings.why: each ray continues the cell's direction from the block centre and reaches the border

readings.reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels. The top-left panel holds a template shape. Every other panel gets the template drawn in the separator colour, and cells already filled there keep their colour.
readings.why: in every non-template panel, the cells that changed are exactly the template cells that were background, and they become the separator colour

readings.reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by separator lines. The top-left panel holds a template shape; in every other panel the template's cells are drawn in the separator colour where the panel is background, keeping cells already there.
readings.why: in every non-template panel, output = input cells plus template positions painted in separator colour

readings.reading: The grid is cut into 3x3 panels by separator lines; the top-left panel holds the template shape. In every panel, template positions that are background are filled with the separator colour; existing cells keep their colour.
readings.why: in every panel, each template position is non-background in the output; cells off the template are unchanged

readings.reading: The grid is 3x3 panels split by separator lines; the top-left panel holds a template shape. In every panel, each template position that is still background is filled with the separator colour; existing cells stay.
readings.why: every background cell at a template offset inside any panel becomes the separator colour (which differs per pair, so the colour is the separator's, not a training constant); nothing else changes

readings.reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by separator lines; the shape in the top-left panel is the template, and in every panel the template positions that are empty are filled with the separator colour, existing cells kept.
readings.why: every background cell at a template position (period 6) becomes the separator colour; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Each L-triomino gets a copy of itself shifted one cell diagonally. A copy of a 5-shape is coloured 4 and shifts toward the empty corner of its 2x2 box. A copy of a 2-shape is coloured 3 and shifts away from it. Copies cover only background, and 3 wins where copies overlap.
readings.why: every changed cell belongs to a diagonally shifted copy of some L, coloured by that L's colour

readings.reading: Background 7 with 3-cell L shapes in grey (5) and red (2). Each red L stamps a copy of itself in colour 3 shifted one cell diagonally through its corner; each grey L stamps a copy in colour 4 shifted one cell diagonally toward its open side. Only background cells are painted; red copies are drawn last.
readings.why: every new cell lies in a one-step diagonal copy of an L in the colour set by that L's colour

readings.reading: Each L-tromino casts a diagonally shifted copy of itself into background cells: grey (5) Ls get a colour-4 copy shifted one step toward the missing corner of their 2x2 box; red (2) Ls get a colour-3 copy shifted one step away from it (3 overrides 4 where they meet).
readings.why: every changed cell is a background cell covered by the diagonal copy of an adjacent L, coloured by the L's colour

readings.reading: Each 3-cell L shape (on background 7) gets a copy of itself shifted one diagonal step: grey-5 L's are copied in colour 4 toward the missing corner of their 2x2 box; red-2 L's are copied in colour 3 away from their missing corner. Copies paint only background cells; where a 3 and a 4 copy overlap, 3 wins.
readings.why: every new cell belongs to the shifted copy of an adjacent L in its mapped colour

readings.reading: Each L-tromino casts a copy of itself shifted one cell diagonally onto background: colour-5 Ls shift into their inner corner and paint 4, colour-2 Ls shift away from their corner and paint 3 (3 wins on overlap).
readings.why: every new cell is a shifted cell of an L, coloured by the L's colour; nothing else changes

readings.reading: A 2x2 block mixes one colour with some 2-cells. Each 2-cell marks a diagonal direction away from the block centre. The whole 2x2 block is swept along each such diagonal to the grid border, all in the block's non-2 colour (the 2-cells take that colour too).
readings.why: the output is exactly the union of the block's repeated diagonal translates in the marked directions, in the non-2 colour

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of colour c with some red (2) cells. The block is swept diagonally toward each red corner to the border, leaving a 3-wide diagonal band of colour c; the red cells become c.
readings.why: the output is the union of the 2x2 block translated by k steps along each red-corner diagonal, all in the non-red colour

readings.reading: A 2x2 block contains some red (2) cells; the block is swept diagonally to the grid border in the direction of each red corner, the whole swept band painted in the block's non-red colour.
readings.why: the output is the union of the block and all its diagonal translates along each red-corner direction, in one colour

readings.reading: A 2x2 block contains some red (2) cells; the block is swept diagonally toward each red cell's corner direction until the grid edge, painting the swept band (and the block itself) in the block's other colour.
readings.why: every output cell of that colour is a cell of the block translated k diagonal steps (k >= 0) in one of the marked directions

readings.reading: A 2x2 block with some red (2) cells slides diagonally toward each red corner to the border, leaving a 2-wide diagonal band in the block's other colour; the block itself becomes that colour.
readings.why: every swept position of the block is filled with the main colour, nothing else

readings.reading: The grid is scaled up by 2. Each 5 cell becomes the 2x2 pattern 12/21, and each background cell becomes a 2x2 background block.
readings.why: output block (i,j) is 12/21 exactly where input cell (i,j) is 5, and empty otherwise

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2: each grey cell becomes the 2x2 block [1 2 / 2 1], each background cell a 2x2 block of 0.
readings.why: every 2x2 output block is the pattern where the input cell is grey and empty otherwise

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2: each grey cell becomes the 2x2 tile [[1,2],[2,1]] and each background cell a 2x2 background tile.
readings.why: output block (i,j) is the fixed tile when input cell (i,j) is non-background, else empty

readings.reading: The 3x3 grid is scaled up by 2: each grey (5) cell becomes the 2x2 tile [1 2 / 2 1] and each 0 cell becomes a 2x2 of 0.
readings.why: output block (r,c) is the fixed tile when input cell (r,c) is 5, else empty

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2; each 5 cell becomes the 2x2 pattern 12/21 and each background cell a 2x2 background block.
readings.why: output block (i,j) is the pattern iff input cell (i,j) is foreground

readings.reading: The top strip has three 3x3 coloured key blocks. The row under it has one mark-colour below each block, which links that mark colour to the block's colour. The output is the area below the separator line, with each mark there replaced by a 3x3 block, centred on it, in the colour its mark-colour is linked to.
readings.why: every 3x3 block in the output is centred on a canvas mark, and its colour equals the key block above the matching key-row mark

readings.reading: Top: three 3x3 colour blocks with one marker cell below each (the legend). Below a full separator row, marker cells are scattered; the output is that lower area with each marker replaced by a 3x3 block centred on it, in the colour the legend gives that marker colour.
readings.why: every 3x3 block in the output sits on a lower-panel marker and has the legend colour of that marker

readings.reading: The top band is a legend: three 3x3 colour blocks with a marker colour under each. Below the separator row, the output is that lower panel with each marker replaced by a 3x3 block (centred on it) of the colour its marker colour is paired with in the legend.
readings.why: output = lower panel background with one 3x3 legend-coloured block centred on every marker

readings.reading: The top panel is a key: three 3x3 colour blocks with one marker pixel under each (row 4), mapping marker colour -> block colour. The output is the bottom panel (below the full separator row), where every marker pixel becomes a 3x3 block of its mapped colour centred on it.
readings.why: every 3x3 block in the output is centred on a marker of the bottom panel and coloured by the key; all other cells are 7

readings.reading: Three 3x3 coloured blocks sit on top, with a key row below each block giving a marker colour; the output is the area below the separator, where every marker is replaced by the block keyed to its colour, centred on the marker, on background 7.
readings.why: each 3x3 block in the output is centred on a lower-panel marker and matches that marker's legend block
